newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Nafta shares gain, halt SAX index slide.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Nafta shares gain, halt SAX index slide.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed on thin volumes on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with gains to Nafta share pushing the 12-share SAX index up 2.16 points to 163.98.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed up 50 crowns at 1,350, but on a volume of eight shares.
"Unfortunately, this means nothing if we look at the volumes of traded shares," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
"There is a package of some 6,000 Nafta shares offered for trade on the bourse, but the current price of about 1,300 crowns is apparently still too high for buyers," he added.
Steel maker VSZ closed up nine crowns at 476, while commercial bank VUB edged up 29 crowns to 1,699.
Overall volume, boosted mainly by direct trades, eased to 205,039 shares, from 237,789 shares traded on Thursday, while turnover fell to 60.03 million crowns, from 185.26 million.
